text: Ledger guests: participants without an account — add, lock, claim on join (design)

Maintainer approved the design; added at their request: guests can be entered in the create-list dialog (dynamic name boxes, no comma parsing) and ride on the creation row as a create-only 'guests' array of names in /sync, ignored on any later push. See 'Guests at list creation' in section 2 and the dialog bullet in section 6.

Groomed: arithmetic checked case by case (unclaimed, claimed, several claimed by one account, guest+claimant on one side, transfer folding to one id, unclaim, departed claimant) — all handled by one fold step before the existing functions; the participant rule now admits claimed guests too (an offline entry racing a claim must not be quarantined); the create-only push key is guest_names, not guests; the freeze stays per stored key (conservative); former-member numbering runs over effective ids; UI placed on the list menu under Members, the create dialog, the form, balances and a post-join chooser.

Claimed by the orchestrator (claude): design groomed, T-365 done, T-366/T-367/T-368 delegated to subagents in worktrees .claude/worktrees/guests-{server,web,android}; this ticket closes with the last of them.

Implemented and landed (T-365..T-368, main up to 17be55cd, protocol 4). Where the code settled something the text did not, the code is the record: Reimburse for a locked guest is hidden, as it is for a voter, not disabled; the web gates the Guests card and the chooser on the list object carrying a guests key (it has no serverProtocol — the bundle ships with its server) and leaves the create-dialog section ungated for the same reason; Android passes the post-join flag through a JoinedLists singleton rather than a route argument; the 'joined' chooser opens only on an open ledger; 'for everyone' on entry rows folds keys first; blank guest names are Cf/Zs-only text, lengths are code points, initials are the first two code points; the shared cases live in their own fold group rather than an aliases field. Release not cut: the maintainer did not ask for one; it will be a major (4.0.0), per section 9.
